package_info.why_malicious: Version 0.0.7 of the 'strong_password' gem is malicious because it contains intentionally obfuscated code that, when loaded in a Rails production environment, spawns a persistent background thread to fetch and execute arbitrary Ruby code from a remote Pastebin URL. This enables remote code execution and backdoor installation. The fetched payload further hooks into Rack middleware to allow attackers to execute arbitrary code via specially crafted HTTP cookies and exfiltrate sensitive environment data to an external server. The malicious code was published via unauthorized access, making the entire package a severe security risk.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time in a Rails production environment, the code spawns a persistent background thread that periodically sleeps for a random interval, fetches Ruby code from a remote Pastebin URL via HTTP, and evaluates it using eval, resulting in remote code execution within the application process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and creates a background thread that repeatedly fetches and executes code from an external source using eval, a classic remote code execution backdoor technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A password strength checking library should never create background threads, perform network requests to untrusted domains, or execute remote code. Such behavior is entirely outside the scope of legitimate functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic code loading from trusted, internal plugin systems may occur in some frameworks, but never in security-sensitive libraries or from untrusted external sources.
key_indicators: Use of eval on HTTP response from external domain
Conditional execution only in production environment (Rails.env[0]=="p")
Background thread for persistent malicious activity

execution_context.trigger: runtime after remote payload is fetched and evaluated

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the remote payload is fetched and evaluated, the code hooks into the Rack::Sendfile middleware by prepending a module that overrides the call method. It inspects incoming HTTP requests for a specially crafted cookie (___id), decodes its value from base64, and evaluates it as Ruby code, enabling arbitrary code execution via HTTP requests. Additionally, it exfiltrates the URL_HOST environment variable to an external server via an HTTP GET request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code dynamically injects itself into Rack middleware to intercept HTTP requests, decodes and evaluates base64-encoded data from a user-supplied cookie, and exfiltrates environment data to an external domain. This is a textbook backdoor pattern allowing remote code execution and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Middleware should never execute code from user-supplied cookies or exfiltrate environment variables. Such actions are a direct abuse of the HTTP request lifecycle and violate all security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for evaluating user-supplied cookie data as code or exfiltrating environment variables in middleware.
key_indicators: Base64-decoded eval on HTTP cookie data (___id)
Dynamic method injection into Rack::Sendfile via Module.prepend
Outbound HTTP request to smiley.zzz.com.ua with environment data
Persistence via global variable (Z1) to prevent re-injection

attack_chain.action: Malicious gem is installed and loaded in a Rails production environment, triggering execution of obfuscated code.
attack_chain.leads_to: A background thread is spawned that periodically fetches and executes remote Ruby code.

attack_chain.action: Background thread fetches Ruby code from Pastebin and evaluates it within the application context.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote payload (snippet_2) is executed, escalating the attack.

attack_chain.action: Remote payload hooks into Rack middleware to intercept HTTP requests and evaluate base64-decoded code from specially crafted cookies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution via HTTP requests containing malicious cookies.

attack_chain.action: Remote payload exfiltrates environment data (URL_HOST) to an external server via HTTP request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive environment information, resulting in full system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or minified Ruby code in gem source files, especially using single-letter method names and rescue blocks
Background threads making periodic HTTP requests to external domains such as pastebin.com
Use of eval on HTTP response bodies or on data extracted from HTTP cookies
Dynamic method injection into Rack middleware using Module.prepend
Base64 decoding and evaluation of HTTP cookie values (e.g., ___id cookie)
file_indicators: lib/strong_password/strength_checker.rb containing obfuscated or minified code
Presence of code that fetches from pastebin.com/raw/xa456PFt or similar external sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Ruby gems, especially version 0.0.7 of strong_password, for obfuscated or minified code that creates background threads, performs network requests to external domains, or uses eval on network responses or HTTP cookie data. Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTP requests to pastebin.com/raw/xa456PFt and smiley.zzz.com.ua. Flag gems that inject methods into Rack middleware or decode and execute data from HTTP cookies. Alert on any gem version containing these patterns, as they indicate a high risk of remote code execution and data exfiltration.
